Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
7 October 2026 .
· Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 gCaptain reports attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest level of any week since the Iran war began, with U.S.-Iran talks still at a stalemate, per International Business Times.

02 An IRGC adviser says Iran will close routes in the strait deemed illegal, per Iranian state media; tanker captains are earning $50,000 per crossing, per the counter-claim in this feed, leaving the transit picture contested.

03 IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; the oil price feed is currently unavailable.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz is registering its most intense period of tanker attacks since the Iran war began. gCaptain reports that strikes on vessels last week reached a new peak for any single week of the conflict, and International Business Times reports U.S.-Iran talks remain at a stalemate as attacks against tankers in the strait reached a record. The oil price feed is dark and no quote is available. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on October 4, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. The closure picture remains actively contested: an IRGC adviser says, per Iranian state media, that routes in the strait deemed illegal will soon be closed and that the waterway will remain shut until Iran's conditions are met, while this feed carries a counter-claim that tanker captains are banking $50,000 per crossing, indicating some transits are occurring. The site's verdict on carrier posture is a cautious closed, but the physical picture is disputed. A retired lieutenant general, cited by MS NOW, warns that not only the Strait of Hormuz but also another key shipping waterway is under threat. This site has indexed 51 events in the last 24 hours across its tracking feeds. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, flagged low-confidence because two of its inputs are stale or missing (the Brent-WTI forward spread and Manifold forward contracts), with Polymarket escalation contracts as its top contributor.
